facts.fact: The IMPULSE study (Nov 2022-Jul 2024) found DHIS2 in use as the routine health information system in central and subnational data offices in Tanzania.

The UDSM DHIS2 Lab states the Ministry of Health has used DHIS2 as its national HMIS to collect routine facility health data since 2010, with datasets managed for about 9,000 health facilities in 184 district councils.

note: Analysis feature; says only that the ministry uses DHIS2 as part of its health information infrastructure, not that facilities across the country report through it.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Health service page lists DHIS2 as the system used for health information collection, storage, analysis, reporting and dissemination, with an HMIS data warehouse accessible through DHIS2 HMIS Data and a public data portal.

note: Chief Medical Officer speech mentions improving data collection through DHIS2 and EMR but does not state a national HMIS is in service, linked, or reports completeness.

facts.fact: The UDSM DHIS2 Lab page says Zanzibar is channelling data from vertical programme systems into the national HMIS (ZHMIS) through the Zanzibar Health Information Layer, led by the Ministry of Health Zanzibar, with a workshop validating end-to-end flows into ZHMIS.

note: No fact on in-service national coverage, linkage to named surveillance, supply-chain or immunisation systems, or reporting rate: the page states none of these.
Document describes surveillance systems only, with no routine health reporting system or its links stated.
An emergency dispatch platform, not the national health reporting system.
Only NHIF's insurance claims system; no national health reporting system stated.
GoTHOMIS is said to link 7,700 facilities but the document does not say it carries routine reporting to the ministry.

facts.fact: A HISP Tanzania paper says the DHIS2 HMIS data warehouse for reporting routine health service data was implemented in Tanzania in 2014, though many facilities still rely on higher-level units to report.

The Citizen, reporting WHO's 2026 assessment, says DHIS2 has been implemented nationally and at district and subnational levels in Tanzania, though information from all health programmes is not yet in a single repository.
